newsitem.title: USA: IMF welcomes Thai talks, sees others involved.
newsitem.headline: IMF welcomes Thai talks, sees others involved.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday welcomed news that Thailand was seeking support to ease its financial crisis and said bilateral support was likely to be part of any future package.

"The authorities have made clear they are looking for an IMF support package," a spokesman said. "Obviously we welcome that news and will be discussing a package with them which will probably involve support both from us and from bilateral sources."

An IMF mission arrived in Thailand at the weekend for talks with the authorities there and officials said they might be looking for an IMF credit line. It would be the first IMF loan to Thailand for over 10 years.
The IMF spokesman said it was too early to speculate on the size of any loan to Thailand or say which countries would join an international package.
Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that Japan would consider a Thai request for funding, for example using loans from Japan's Export-Import Bank.
